outcome.technical: ONE HELPER: tests/_harness.py gains growth_series(call, inputs, clock=time.perf_counter, clock_name='perf_counter', steps=GROWTH_STEPS, min_seconds=GROWTH_MIN_SECONDS, rounds=3, deadline=60.0, wall=time.perf_counter) and clock_step(). It repeats call(x) in batches until a batch's total on `clock` is at least floor = max(steps * max(get_clock_info(clock_name).resolution, measured step), min_seconds); the step is measured by clock_step (reading the clock until it changes, least of three steps from an edge). Rounds take the inputs in turn; a round counts only when its batch reached the floor; per input the least per-call round is kept. It returns {seconds (per call), repeats, totals, floor, resolution, fault}; fault is None, or a sentence naming the input by place and length, the floor and the deadline when an input could not reach `rounds` batches at the floor before `deadline` seconds of `wall`, or 'the clock did not advance' when clock_step sees no change in CLOCK_PROBE_SECONDS. A faulted series holds only the inputs before the first unmeasured one. GROWTH_STEPS = 10: at the floor a doubling reads within (steps-1)/(steps+1) and its inverse of its size, so a linear doubling reads under 2 ** 1.5 while a 1/64 s series fits the children's deadlines. CONSUMERS: cw8's child (tests/test__clause_coverage.py _WIDE_TIMER) and esc53's python child (tests/test_build_shop.py _PY_TIMER) import _harness from TESTS_DIR and call growth_series inside the child, so the child is still the unit killed at WIDE_DEADLINE / TRIPWIRE_DEADLINE; neither keeps a private loop. New per-case parameters: WIDE_SERIES_DEADLINE 45.0, WIDE_MIN_SECONDS 0.02, WIDE_ROUNDS 3 (HEAD's loop took 3 rounds); TRIPWIRE_MIN_SECONDS 0.01, TRIPWIRE_ROUNDS 3 (HEAD's min_rounds), TRIPWIRE_SERIES_DEADLINE 8.0. A helper fault is a case fault worded 'could not be measured: <sentence>'; timer_answer accepts a faulted line. esc53's clock moved from perf_counter to process_time: helper batches on perf_counter still read 4.21x (18:18, load 20) and 4.83x (18:22, load 29, 10 cores) under local load, while process_time under load 29 read 2.13x (measured once under that load; 2.10-2.12x in three later runs under load 3-13). esc55 (node) keeps its own loop: it is another engine and passed on windows. NO threshold moved: WIDE_POWER/FLOOR/CEILING/BYTES/DEADLINE, TRIPWIRE_POWER/FLOOR/CEILING/DEADLINE and gw15's ratio < 6 are unchanged. SAME FAULT ELSEWHERE: of the process_time/perf_counter readers in tests/, gw15 (tests/test_guard_history_rewrite.py, outside the declared files) went red under the coarse clock ('fastest at 4 operands 0.0 s, at 16 0.0 s, ratio unmeasurable'), so it was moved to growth_series (min_seconds 0.005, rounds 5) and its now-unused `import time` removed; the plan gate allowed the edit. fx6 (tests/test__floor_guard.py) was run under the coarse clock and stayed green (a 10 s ceiling over a ~1.1 s run), so it was left alone. RUNS: the gate command above exit 0 (4/4 files, 329 cases); sweep --selftest exit 0 (168/168); the orchestrator's gate unrecorded: GATE GREEN, exit 0; ruff and vermin -t=3.8- clean on the four changed suites; prose_number_claims() and house_style_violations() report nothing. Suite seconds (sweep --jobs 1), before on a HEAD export at 18:12 (load 11.7) and 18:42 (load 2.8), after at 18:43 (load 3.1) and 19:09 (load 3.0): _harness 9.0/9.0 -> 9.1/9.1; test__clause_coverage 4.3/4.3 -> 5.3/5.2; test_build_shop 10.4/10.7 -> 12.2/12.9; test_guard_history_rewrite 0.8 (once at HEAD) -> 0.8/0.8. On a 1/64 s clock (windows' real process-time step) the cw8 child takes 12.6 s and esc53's 18 python children 40.3 s (19:10, load 3.5), against about 2.2 s and 3.1 s on the real clock here. A mutation probe (scratchpad sg2.7/mutations.py, 25 rows, exit 0) holds the before/after coarse-clock rows, the quadratic reading and backtracking tripwire on both clocks, the zero series deadlines, and one row per helper rule. DEPENDANTS: tests/_harness.py's importers and the names used elsewhere (_group_present, _load_sweep, _pid_present, _positive_int) are untouched, since the change only adds names; the prose mentions in tests/test__refs.py and tools/sweep-selftests.py still hold. tests/test__affected_tests.py and tools/sweep-selftests.py are unchanged and green. test__clause_coverage.py's and test_build_shop.py's path mentions (.github/sweep-costs.json, _clause_coverage.py, the eval case.yaml files, tests/test__output_lints.py, CHANGELOG.md, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md) are unaffected, and _cases/_selftest/write_hook/tool_result are unchanged. .github/sweep-costs.json now underweights both suites on windows (not a declared file; not edited).
outcome.descriptive: cw8, esc53 and gw15 now take their growth series from one harness helper that repeats each call until the batch is long enough for the clock's measured step, so a 1/64 s clock neither turns them red (cw8, gw15) nor green on all-zero readings (esc53); a series the helper cannot measure before its deadline fails, naming what was not measured.
